name: FlipFlop
summary: D-type and RS-type flip-flop: Clk, In, Rst, Q and NotQ.
author: Animatek
about: A flip-flop remembers one bit. It has two types, picked by the Type button: D-type and RS-type. Q is the stored bit and NotQ its opposite.

D-type: on each rising edge of Clk, Q takes whatever In is at that moment. RS-type: a rising edge on In sets Q; with In low, each rising edge of Clk toggles Q. Rst, when high, clears Q in both types and wins over everything else.
usage: Clock a D-type from an LFO or a sequencer's gate and feed In from another gate: Q samples it on every clock.
Choose RS and leave In unplugged: every clock edge toggles Q, so it divides the clock by two.
Use Rst to bring several flip-flops back in step at the start of a bar.
notes: Control rate: good for gates and slow logic, not for audio. The example patch flipflop-lfo.pch clocks it from an LFO.
